title: Herb's Hideout
venue_description:
Denver's Historic Music Dive

Herb's Hideout is a legendary Denver music venue housed in a historic tavern erected in 1933. Located at 2057 Larimer Street in the heart of LoDo this authentic dive bar has maintained its character through decades of Denver's evolution serving as a respite from gentrification while hosting some of the city's best live music.

History and Awards

Over its long tenure Herb's has worn many hats: dive bar cougar bar live-music dance hall and neighborhood gathering place. The venue has earned multiple Best of Denver awards including Best Bar in LoDo to Pretend You're on Colfax (2025) Best Unpretentious Yet Legendary Venue (2023) Best Blues Jam (2010) and Best Place to Get Away and Get Down (2002).

The Space

The venue features a small intimate stage perfect for close-up musical experiences. The dimly lit cozy atmosphere creates an authentic dive bar feel with no pretensions. Despite its location near LoDo's more gentrified areas Herb's maintains its working-class roots and welcoming unpretentious vibe.

Music Programming

Herb's hosts live music six nights a week with a diverse lineup that has included everyone from local underground acts to nationally touring artists. Monday nights feature regular performers. Tuesday nights are known for excellent jazz performances that are highly favored by regulars. Wednesdays host the popular all-genre open jam starting at 9:30 PM with full backline provided. Thursdays feature regular performers. Fridays and Saturdays showcase Pop/Rock/Top 40 bands starting at 9:30 PM.

The Wednesday Open Jam

The weekly open jam has become one of Denver's most popular musician gatherings. The venue provides complete backline including drums bass guitar and PA system. Musicians can sign up when doors open at 9:30 PM and the jam runs until 1:30 AM. The event is completely free with no cover charge. The atmosphere is judgment-free and welcoming to all skill levels and genres.

Drinks and Atmosphere

Herb's is known for reasonably priced stiff drinks served by friendly staff in a welcoming environment. The bar features a good selection of local beers and well-crafted cocktails. Midnight happy hour runs from midnight to 1:30 AM offering great deals for late-night performers and attendees. Free cheese puffs are available at the bar.

Hours and Access

The venue operates Monday through Wednesday 6 PM to 2 AM and Friday through Sunday 3 PM to 2 AM. The location is accessible with a wheelchair-accessible entrance available though the venue maintains its classic dive-style layout with limited table service. Street parking is available though it can be scarce during peak hours.

Community and Culture

Described as musician-owned Herb's walls have absorbed decades of Denver's musical stories. The venue maintains strong connections to Denver's independent and underground music scenes. Regular patrons praise the friendly staff sense of community and authentic atmosphere that keeps them coming back. This is a place where you can get away from corporate chains and experience real Denver music culture.

title: Swallow Hill Music
venue_description:
Denver's Community Music School and Jam Session Hub

Swallow Hill Music is a nonprofit community music school located at 71 E Yale Avenue in Denver operating as the city's premier destination for acoustic music education and community jam sessions. With a tradition dating back to the 1960s as part of the Denver Folklore Center Swallow Hill represents one of America's longest-running acoustic music institutions.

History and Mission

Open jam sessions at Swallow Hill have been a tradition since the venue's beginnings as part of the Denver Folklore Center in the 1960s. As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization (Tax ID: 84-0781725) Swallow Hill's mission extends beyond music education to community building through shared musical experiences. The organization operates with support from the Scientific and Cultural Facilities District (SCFD).

Facilities

The building features multiple performance and teaching spaces. Weekly jams are held in the Quinlan Cafe downstairs providing an intimate welcoming atmosphere perfect for collaborative music-making. Monthly genre-specific jams utilize various rooms throughout the building. The venue offers quality acoustics accessible facilities and a cafe that operates during concerts and special events Thursday through Sunday from 4 PM to 9 PM.

Comprehensive Jam Session Programming

Swallow Hill offers Denver's most extensive jam session schedule with programs for nearly every acoustic music tradition. All jams are led by expert instructors and community members who create welcoming all-levels-welcome environments.

Weekly Jam Sessions

Monday Night Jam (8 PM): Led by Spencer Erik Crawford this multi-genre jam knows no boundaries covering everything from Zydeco to Prince's Greatest Hits to bluegrass classics to Top 40 AM Gold. Spencer calls out chords and changes while encouraging students to lead tunes when they feel called. A perfect way to kick off your week with eclectic musical exploration.

Tuesday Night Jam (8 PM): Led by Mike Jagel this storied session has decades of Swallow Hill lore behind it. Mike brings beautiful charts of SH standards cowboy classics and bluegrass favorites while encouraging students to bring their own charts of songs they want to lead. Mike keeps time and brings out the best in both beginner jammers and experienced players.

Monthly Jam Sessions

Bluegrass Jam (4th Sundays 2-4 PM): Led by Virginia Anderson this informal collaborative setting welcomes anyone to try out songs they've been working on or learn new material. Perfect for getting direction on technique performance and song repertoire in traditional bluegrass style.

Jazz Jam (2nd Sundays 2-4 PM): Led by Felix Ayodele each session begins by examining a key portion of a jazz standard planning how to improvise over the changes then giving everyone a chance to put theory into practice. Beginners learn the full scope of music knowledge waiting while advanced players deepen their theory and swap tricks. Everyone gets to solo and build confidence. Drum set available with one day advance notice by calling (303) 777-1003.

Old-Time Jam (3rd Sundays 1-3 PM): Led by Jake Loew this jam celebrates Southern Appalachian and broader old-time repertoire and traditions. While centered on acoustic guitars banjos and fiddles all instruments are welcome. The session explores how old-time music exists and evolves in modern times through a unique and special community approach.

Irish Jam (1st Sundays 1-3 PM): Led by John Hammer this beginner/intermediate traditional Irish-style music session is sheet music friendly. Bring a tune or two and your instrument - all instruments and songs are welcome in this supportive setting.

Circle Singing (3rd Saturdays 2-3:30 PM): Led by Roy Willey this community singing and sounding practice is spontaneous and evolving like a drum circle for voices. Based on practices developed by Bobby McFerrin this is a supportive judgment-free space to play with your voice through improvised vocal grooves and patterns. All voices welcome.

Denver Uke Community (3rd Saturdays 10:30 AM-1 PM): Open to all ukulele players of any skill level this monthly gathering brings uke players together to share songs in a supportive group setting. For more information visit www.den-uke.com.

Clawhammer Corner (Last Thursdays 6-7 PM): Led by Caleb James Hall this online jam via Zoom welcomes clawhammer banjo players of all levels to meet up and share things they're working on learn from each other and discuss techniques and inspirations.

Tabla Jam (4th Saturdays 10 AM-1 PM): Led by Nabin Shrestha these three-hour sessions explore the sounds and language of the Tabla - the iconic pair of twin hand drums of North Indian heritage. Open to Tabla players new students percussionists and non-percussionists interested in Hindustani and other musical genres featuring this instrument.

What Musicians Get

Access to Denver's longest-running jam session tradition spanning six decades. Expert instruction and facilitation by accomplished community musicians. A supportive all-levels-welcome environment where mistakes are part of learning. Connection to Denver's thriving acoustic music community across multiple genres. Quality acoustics and welcoming spaces designed for collaborative music-making.

Donation Model

To sustain the jam sessions Swallow Hill asks for a suggested minimum donation of $10 per attendee. Donations can be made online or in-person at jams and directly support the teachers and music school programs. This accessible pricing ensures jams remain available to all while supporting the nonprofit's mission.

Additional Programs

Beyond jam sessions Swallow Hill offers extensive music classes for all ages and skill levels progressive 4-month intensives summer camps outreach programs including Little Swallows music therapy team building programs and a full concert series featuring local national and international artists. The organization also provides tuition assistance to ensure music education remains accessible.

Hours and Contact

Front desk hours are Monday-Thursday 12 PM to 9 PM and during live events plus Friday-Sunday during live events only. The cafe operates during concerts and special events Thursday-Sunday 4 PM to 9 PM. Contact (303) 777-1003 or email info@swallowhillmusic.org for questions about upcoming jams or other programs.

title: Lion's Lair
venue_description:
Denver's Iconic Dive Bar and Music Venue

Lion's Lair is a legendary dive bar and music venue located at 2022 E Colfax Avenue in Denver established in 1969. For over 50 years this iconic venue has been a cornerstone of Denver's independent music scene hosting thousands of acts and maintaining an authentic unpretentious atmosphere that has made it a beloved institution.

History and Legacy

Since opening in 1969 Lion's Lair has hosted an impressive roster of national and international touring acts including Jonathan Richman Detroit Cobras Sleepy LaBeef Chris Whitley Slim Cessna's Auto Club DeVotchKa The Decemberists The White Stripes The Black Keys John Doe G. Love and Special Sauce Reverend Horton Heat Cracker Camper Van Beethoven Apples in Stereo Turbonegro Jim Carroll and Lydia Lunch among many others. The venue has also been a launching pad for countless local Denver bands including Lyin' Bitch & The Restraining Orders.

Awards and Recognition

Lion's Lair has earned multiple Best of Denver awards including Best Open-Mic Night (2025 Readers' Choice) recognizing its Wednesday night music open mic as Denver's premier opportunity for emerging artists to perform and develop their craft.

The Venue

Lion's Lair embodies the classic dive bar aesthetic - dimly lit cozy and unpretentious with a small intimate stage that creates close connections between performers and audience. The venue maintains its authentic character serving affordable canned beers well cocktails and offering an edgy intimate nightlife vibe. The space features a wheelchair-accessible entrance and restroom though it operates with casual standing and bar seating rather than table service.

Weekly Music Programming

Wednesday Open Mic (8 PM-11:59 PM): Denver's hottest open stage featuring a showcase set from local or touring bands at 8 PM followed by open mic starting at 9 PM. Complete backline provided including drums guitar bass and PA system. Sign-up begins when doors open at 7 PM. The event is completely free to attend with midnight happy hour running from midnight to 1:30 AM offering great deals on drinks. The venue provides a judgment-free zone for musicians to rock their songs in front of a supportive audience.

Thursday-Sunday Nights: Live music featuring diverse local and touring acts spanning punk rock indie and alternative genres. The small stage creates an intimate energetic atmosphere perfect for high-energy performances.

Second Tuesday: Live music with Coverboy providing regular monthly programming.

Other Weekly Events

Monday Nights (10 PM sign-up 10:30 PM start): Open Mic Comedy Night hosted by Anthony Crawford. Comedians get 7 minutes with only 2 guaranteed spots. No cover charge for this popular comedy showcase.

Sunday Nights (9 PM): Karaoke at Lion's Lair with an expansive song selection. Perfect opportunity to unleash your inner rockstar in front of a supportive crowd.

Saturday Afternoons (2-6 PM): Kooky Kitsch with DJ Frank Bell providing eclectic afternoon entertainment.

What Musicians Get

Complete professional backline including drums guitar bass and full PA system. An authentic judgment-free performance environment. Connection to Denver's legendary underground and independent music scene. Midnight happy hour for performers and attendees. Affordable drinks in a classic dive bar setting. Access to a venue with over 50 years of music history and a track record of launching careers.

Atmosphere and Culture

Lion's Lair is celebrated by regulars for its authentic dive bar atmosphere friendly staff vibrant live music scene and strong sense of community. The venue attracts a diverse crowd of music enthusiasts who appreciate the unpretentious vibe and quality of performances. Early evening (before 10 PM) offers the best prices on domestic beers and cocktails.

Best Times to Visit

For live punk and open mic nights arrive after 8 PM on weekdays. Weekends from 7 PM feature the liveliest crowds and full band lineups. The Wednesday open jam starting at 8:30 PM is particularly popular among musicians and fans of live local music.

Practical Information

The venue opens at 6 PM Monday-Wednesday and 3 PM Thursday-Sunday running until 2 AM nightly. Street parking is available but can be scarce during weekend peak hours - arrive early for best spots. Cash is recommended for smoother transactions. The venue is located on Denver's famous Colfax Avenue making it easily accessible and part of the city's cultural corridor.

Booking

For booking inquiries email girlwreckpresents@gmail.com. The venue continues to book diverse acts maintaining its reputation as one of Denver's most important independent music venues.
